messages:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] kv-cache memory cliff detected in prod-west-1: sustained GPU mem usage spike + OOMs across multiple pods — severity: P1. Auto-escalation to oncall.
Maya (oncall): seeing it, joining. agree this looks like the continuous-batching path. metrics: eviction_rate x10, avg-batch-size spiked.
Maya (oncall): @Jun can you confirm if the new batching cap rollout touched prod-west yesterday?
Jun (eng-runtime): we rolled a config bump to continuous_batch.max_tokens=4096 -> 8192 at 03:12 UTC for canary -> gradually to prod. Canary looked fine.
Oliver (eng-ml): perf test showed compaction regressions with long prefixes and quantized cache entries; might exacerbate fragmentation.
Rachel (sre): customer impact: several webhooks reporting +500 latencies, a few 503s. CS says two enterprise tenants reported errors. tagging CustomerOps.
CustomerOps: confirmed two customers got increased error rates, ticket opened INC-4729. Need ETA on mitigation.
Jun (eng-runtime): grabbing logs. initial error in pod gpu-23: "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" followed by multiple retries and then eviction thrash. snippet:
```
E 2026-03-15T03:45:12Z runtime.cpp:624 cudaMalloc(ptr=0x7f3a...) -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
W 2026-03-15T03:45:13Z kv_cache.cpp:312 eviction triggered, evicted_slots=512
E 2026-03-15T03:45:14Z batcher.cpp:207 unexpected batch growth: size=16384 tokens
```
Maya (oncall): ops plan: 1) throttle continuous batching globally (reduce max_tokens to 2048) 2) revert the rollout if throttle doesn't help 3) apply arena tweak to reduce fragmentation pressure. I'll apply throttle now.
Maya (oncall): /run ops-bot set-config continuous_batch.max_tokens=2048 --scope=prod-west-1
Ops-Bot: config change applied to prod-west-1: continuous_batch.max_tokens=2048, rollout id=rb-20260315-01 :rocket: 
Rachel (sre): tracking OOMs and latencies on dash. initial drop in OOM count after config change?
Jun (eng-runtime): preliminary: OOMs dropped ~60% in last 3m but eviction rate still elevated. batch-size distribution tightened.
Oliver (eng-ml): canary shows less fragmentation but underlying allocator arenas still have high free-slab fragmentation. we should run a targeted arena compaction on affected hosts.
Maya (oncall): agree. Jun, can you schedule a controlled compaction? Need safe procedure to avoid evict storms.
Jun (eng-runtime): proposing rolling compaction: pause new large batches on a host, run arena.compact(force=true, threshold=0.25), wait for metrics stable, unpause. scripting now.
Jun (eng-runtime): script snippet:
```
# safe compaction
curl -X POST /admin/hosts/gpu-23/pause_batches
python tools/arena_compact.py --host gpu-23 --threshold 0.25 --wait
curl -X POST /admin/hosts/gpu-23/unpause_batches
```
Maya (oncall): execute on two least-loaded nodes first. Rachel, coordinate maintenance window for ~5min windows per host.
Rachel (sre): doing it. Scheduling compaction windows at :50 and :56 for two hosts. Notifying paging rotations.
CustomerOps: communicated mitigation steps to impacted customers, asked for timeframe ~30-60m.
Jun (eng-runtime): compaction run on gpu-23 started. monitor shows freed_pages +12% but we had one transient latency bump during pause.
Maya (oncall): note: avoid full restart of serving processes; restarts spike cold-KV loads and worsen thing. prefer in-place compaction.
Oliver (eng-ml): as medium-term: we should add a guard to prevent batch growth when eviction_rate > X and add a fallback to smaller model-variant for large sequences.
Maya (oncall): escalation: if OOMs persist after two compactions and throttle, we'll rollback the config change to previous max_tokens and open an RCA.
Jun (eng-runtime): compaction on second host completed, GPU mem fragmentation down ~8%, eviction rate trending down.
Rachel (sre): customer-visible errors falling, 503s back to typical baseline. marking incident as mitigation-in-progress.
IncidentBot: [UPDATE] Severity remains P1 until stable for 30m without OOM regressions. Next auto-check in 15m.
Maya (oncall): filing hotfix PR to cap batch growth at runtime and add an immediate circuit-breaker when cudaMalloc fails repeatedly. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/6123
Oliver (eng-ml): leaving a note to perf team: run long-prefix quantization tests with the new cap; monitor KV fragmentation curves.
Maya (oncall): thumbs up. temporary mitigations look effective. I'll stay on the thread for now. If anything new, ping me. :thumbsup:
CustomerOps: customers acknowledged update and appreciate the proactive mitigation.
Maya (oncall): closing loop: postmortem plan: collect allocator traces, batch histograms, and rollout timeline. Owner: Jun. Target draft in 72h.
Jun (eng-runtime): acknowledged. collecting traces now.
Maya (oncall): thanks everyone. will update incident status to 'mitigated' after 30m stable window.
